stories.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
stories.summary: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including the latest on Kawhi Leonard and the NBA's investigation into the Clippers.
stories.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Sept. 10

Justice Department opens criminal inquiry into Clippers' dealings with Leonard
The U.S. Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into the LA Clippers, The New York Times reported Thursday evening, looking at how the team allegedly arranged secret sponsorship contracts for Leonard.

The probe is being conducted by the U.S. attorney's office in Brooklyn, New York.

Sept. 8

Pelicans trade Hawkins to Grizzlies in four-player deal
The New Orleans Pelicans have traded Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Memphis Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday.

The trade clears roster space for the Pelicans, frees up salary flexibility to sign Bennedict Mathurin to a two-year, $16 million deal, and allows the team to have a look at a young player in Johnson, who was the No. 21 pick in the 2023 NBA draft. Hawkins, a lottery pick at No. 14 in the same draft, now gets dealt by his team prior to his fourth season.

Sept. 4

Ben Simmons signs with Kings on one-year deal
Three-time All-Star Ben Simmons has agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Sacramento Kings, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The deal marks a return to the NBA for Simmons, who sat out the 2025-26 season. Simmons was the No. 1 pick in the 2016 NBA draft.

Sept. 3

Windhorst: Steve Ballmer 'very' angry after NBA penalty
ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported that LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is 'very angry' after the penalties handed down to the franchise by the NBA on Sept. 2.

"When you're worth $150 billion and you're angry, and he's very clearly angry, you can't advise him, you can't talk to him," Windhorst said on Get Up. "I'd be stunned if his lawyers didn't advise him, as Shams [Charania] said, to make a plea deal because he should've made a please deal."

Read more: NBA punishes Clippers after Kawhi investigation: Top questions​

Thompson, Rockets agree to five-year contract extension
The Houston Rockets and Amen Thompson have agreed to a five-year, $208 million rookie-scale contract extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania The deal includes a 10% trade kicker.

Sept. 2

NBA insiders answer the biggest questions on NBA's Clippers investigation
After the NBA released the findings of its yearlong investigation into allegations that the LA Clippers circumvented the salary cap in order to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard, ESPN NBA insiders Baxter Holmes, Brian Windhorst, Ramona Shelburne and Bobby Marks examined the report, the massive punishments the NBA leveled and how all of it could impact this season -- and beyond.

The punishment was compounded by the Clippers being previous offenders during Steve Ballmer's tenure as owner. They were fined $250,000 for a similar accusation involving DeAndre Jordan in 2015. There also was a 2019 investigation into Leonard's signing in which the Clippers were cleared of wrongdoing but subsequently warned and put through a seminar to remind them of the rules.
This penalty is indeed harsh, but it could have been worse.

In the case of Joe Smith and the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2000, his contract was voided and his Bird rights were vacated.

Leonard will have to write a sizable check -- $700,000 -- but he will not be suspended, and his contract and Bird rights remain unaffected.

The Clippers and the Toronto Raptors will be allowed to move forward in their trade process, one league source said. If the trade moves forward, LA will acquire two first-round picks in the deal. -- Windhorst

Read the full story here.

Charania: NBA rules on Kawhi Leonard-Aspiration investigation
Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania reported that, after a year-long probe into Kawhi Leonard-Aspiration connection, the NBA has stripped the LA Clippers of five first-round picks and issued a $30 million fine to owner Steve Ballmer, as well as suspended Ballmer, Lawrence Frank and Gillian Zucker.

On top of that, Leonard will have to pay $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits by the franchise for his uncle and former business representative, Dennis Robertson. Leonard will not be suspended but Robertson is banned by the NBA from all business dealings.

SEC requesting information from Daktronics regarding Clippers probe
The Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from Daktronics, the company that designed the LA Clippers' videoboard inside the Intuit Dome, related to Kawhi Leonard, a company executive said Wednesday.

"Let me now briefly address a matter that has been in the media concerning the NBA's investigation of Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers in connection with the league's collective bargaining agreement that many of you may have heard about," chief financial officer Howard Atkins said on Daktronics' quarterly earnings call.

"As you might expect, we have received requests for information from the NBA. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from us concerning the company and Mr. Leonard. "We take these requests seriously and are cooperating. At this point, out of respect for the respective processes, we will not be providing further comment."

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment.

Podcaster Pablo Torre reported last month that Daktronics had an undisclosed sponsorship agreement allegedly worth millions of dollars with Leonard.

Torre interviewed someone identified as an "anonymous high-level source under contract for Intuit Dome" who alleged that the sponsorship deal "was 1,000% a way to circumvent the salary cap. It was funneling money from the Clippers through Daktronics back to Kawhi."

The NBA launched its investigation into the Clippers and Leonard last September after numerous podcasts from Torre, who cited internal documents that showed that Clippers owner Steve Ballmer invested $50 million in Aspiration, a now-defunct green banking company, through his personal LLC in September 2021.

That month, the Clippers signed a 23-year, $300 million deal with Aspiration, making the company the "first founding partner" of the Intuit Dome.

Six months later, Aspiration signed its $28 million endorsement deal with Leonard.

An unnamed employee who purportedly worked for the banking company told Torre that Leonard's sponsorship deal "was to circumvent the salary cap."

The Clippers have repeatedly denied that they funneled money through Aspiration to compensate Leonard.

On Aug. 17, ESPN reported that the NBA has found no evidence showing Ballmer funneled money through team sponsors to pay Leonard in order to circumvent the salary cap, per three people with knowledge of recent discussions between the two sides. -- Baxter Holmes

Sept. 1

Windhorst: Sabonis hired new agent this summer, could want out of Sacramento

On the Sept. 1 episode of "The Hoop Collective," ESPN's Brian Windhorst discussed what Domantas Sabonis hiring a new agent this summer could mean for his future with the Sacramento Kings.

Windhorst on Sabonis hiring a new agent: " I do think it's somewhat interesting that he changed agents this offseason. He hired Aaron Mintz of CAA. Steve Heumann and that group. One of the top executives at CAA. This last year, Mintz and his group executed the trade for Trae Young away from Atlanta, executed the trade for Walker Kessler away from the [Jazz]. Domantas Sabonis just hired him.

"At the risk of ... parodying myself from the season, why would he do that?"

Aug. 29

Latest on Curry's next deal decision

The window for Stephen Curry to sign an extension has officially opened.

The four-time champion and two-time MVP is now eligible (through June 30) to sign a two-year, $136.7 million extension. If he signs, Curry will become the first player in NBA history to rack up more than $600 million in on-court earnings.

A new contract for Curry will have important financial implications for Golden State. With Curry, Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III able to become free agents after the 2026-27 season, Golden State could have significant cap space to reshape its roster.

If Curry signs for the maximum allowed in the first season of an extension ($65.7 million), the Warriors project to have between $45 million and $60 million in cap space next offseason. -- Bobby Marks

Wolves, Jazz swap forwards
The Minnesota Timberwolves are trading forward Josh Green to the Utah Jazz for forwards Cody Williams and John Konchar, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

The Wolves are expected to keep Williams, the No. 10 pick in 2024, and waive-and-stretch Konchar, sources said. By moving Green's $14.7 million salary, Minnesota can sign Jonathan Kuminga to the taxpayer midlevel exception.

Aug. 27

Free agent center Richards agrees to one-year deal with Heat
Free agent center Nick Richards has agreed to a one-year deal with the Miami Heat, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. After signing Klay Thompson, the Heat fill roster slot No. 14 with a reserve big man.

Aug. 26

Kuminga signs two-year deal with Minnesota
Free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Kuminga probably will start alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert.

Mathurin to sign with Pels
Free agent guard Bennedict Mathurin agreed to a two-year, $16 million deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, including a player option, sources tell ESPN.

Aug. 25

Warriors agree to deal with Niang

Forward Georges Niang agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Golden State Warriors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Warriors sign guard Williams
Free agent guard Brandon Williams is signing a one-year, $2.6M deal with the Golden State Warriors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Williams averaged 13 points and 3.9 assists per game last season for the Dallas Mavericks.

Aug. 24

Blazers lose Sharpe to injury
Portland Trail Blazers guard Shaedon Sharpe sustained a torn meniscus in his right knee, and he is expected to miss six months, sources told ESPN.

Sharpe, 23, averaged 20.8 points for the Blazers last season but missed a large chunk of the campaign with a stress fracture of his left fibula.

His four-year, $90 million extension, which he signed last year, officially kicks in this season. Sharpe will make $20.1 million in 2026-27.

Aug. 21

Nuggets signing DeRozan to one-year deal
Six-time NBA All-Star DeMar DeRozan agreed to sign with the Denver Nuggets on a one-year, $3.9 million deal, sources told ESPN on Friday.

DeRozan landed on the Nuggets after speaking to the Miami Heat, Washington Wizards and New Orleans Pelicans during free agency, choosing a significant role in Denver and a chance to compete in the West. The Nuggets' front office and coaches made a strong recruitment effort in recent weeks to secure DeRozan's commitment, showing him how he would complement Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray as an additional playmaker. He also gives the Nuggets a veteran backcourt presence after sending young, versatile wing Peyton Watson to Cleveland as part of a four-team trade.

Mavs buy out Thompson, to sign with Heat
Klay Thompson is expected to sign with the Miami Heat after clearing waivers following his contract buyout from the Dallas Mavericks, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

Thompson, 36, was due to make $17.5 million in the final season of his contract with the Mavericks, who announced his buyout Friday afternoon.

He played two seasons for the Mavericks, averaging 12.9 points per game and shooting 38.7% from 3-point range. Thompson passed Damian Lillard last season to rank fourth in career 3-pointers made.

Aug. 20

Harden to return to Cavs
Free agent James Harden agreed to sign a three-year, $97M contract to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

The Cavs acquired Harden, who turns 37 on Aug. 26, from the LA Clippers in early February in a trade for guard Darius Garland. Cleveland went 21-9 after Harden debuted, tied for the fifth-best record after Feb. 7, as he averaged 20.5 points, 7.7 assists and 4.8 rebounds per game after the All-Star break.

Aug. 19

Watson to Cavs in multiteam trade
The Cleveland Cavaliers, Denver Nuggets and LA Clippers agreed on a trade sending Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers, Max Strus to LA, and an unprotected 2031 Cavs first-round pick and 2032 Sacramento Kings second-rounder to the Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. As part of the trade, the Cavaliers will send Tre Mann to the Washington Wizards for Cam Whitmore and a 2027 second-round pick.

Watson will sign a new four-year, $88 million deal with Cleveland.

Aug. 17

Suns, Highsmith agree to one-year deal

The Phoenix Suns and forward Haywood Highsmith agreed to a one-year deal, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Watford, Pelicans agree to one-year deal
Free agent forward Trendon Watford agreed to a one-year, $2.9 million deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Watford, 25, considered multiple options, but for New Orleans he serves as a productive two-way get late into the offseason.

Aug. 14

Cavaliers trade Schroder, cash to Hornets for Mann
The Cleveland Cavaliers are trading Dennis Schroder and cash to the Charlotte Hornets for Tre Mann, sources told ESPN on Friday.

The Hornets, Cavaliers and Schroder's rep, Mark Bartelstein of Priority Sports, worked for the past couple months on the deal, which also provides Cleveland flexibility to continue pursuing roster moves and tax savings to keep the team well under the second apron, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

Aug. 13

Beal re-signs with Clippers
Free agent guard Bradley Beal agreed to a two-year, $13.2 million deal to return to the LA Clippers, with a player option in the second season, Mark Bartelstein of Priority Sports told ESPN.

After declining his $5.6 million player option, Beal sifted through options over the last month in free agency, including interest from the Miami Heat, before landing on the Clippers. He returns to LA after rehabbing from hip surgery that cost him all but six games last season.

Aug. 12
Westbrook announces retirement from NBA
Russell Westbrook, the 2017 MVP, a nine-time All-NBA selection and the league's all-time triple-double leader, is retiring from the NBA, the 37-year-old announced on Wednesday. Westbrook had contract offers this offseason from the Sacramento Kings and Washington Wizards but chose to step away on his own terms, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Drafted No. 4 overall by the Seattle SuperSonics in 2008 just before the franchise relocated to Oklahoma City, Westbrook played 11 of his 18 seasons with the Thunder. The electric guard and Hall of Fame lock then spent the remainder of his career with the Houston Rockets, Wizards, Los Angeles Lakers, LA Clippers, Denver Nuggets and Kings.

Westbrook retires with the fifth most assists in NBA history (10,351).

NBA world praises 'legendary' career

Aug. 11

McMenamin: NBA excited to grow product with 3 p.m. opening day tip-off
ESPN's Dave McMenamin went on NBA Today to discuss the recent schedule release for the NBA's opening day and Christmas games.

"I've talked to people around the league today and they're like we could sense the excitement for the NBA right now. So let's experiment with this thing," McMenamin said. "They talked with executives at NBC, and it was kind of a joint decision that this is something we can turn into a celebration of the game. It's already a marquee moment for the league. Let's see if we can enhance it and turn it into a major showcase. Maybe down the line, this becomes a tradition for NBA fans. ... [Also the NBA is] an international game. 3 p.m. Eastern is primetime viewing in Europe."

The Boston Celtics and Detroit Pistons open the season on Tuesday, Oct. 20 at 3 p.m. ET on NBA/Peacock.

What's latest on Kawhi and the Clippers? And updates on Nuggets, Suns
Brian is joined by ESPN's Anthony Slater to discuss the latest in the ongoing Kawhi Leonard-LA Clippers situation, including how it could impact the Toronto Raptors and the Eastern Conference during the 2026-27 season. They move on to the cover the Dillon Brooks' contract and how it impacts the future spending plans for the Phoenix Suns. The duo then closes on how the Denver Nuggets' books put them in trouble moving forward, and a remembrance of Don Nelson.

Windhorst on the newest Kawhi Leonard situation: "That's obviously key: Did he get money from Daktronics? Slater, if this is accurate, the Clippers side of it is devastating.
But let's put that aside for right now. For the actual business of the NBA for the 26-27 season, this is not just a Clipper issue. Last year was a Clipper issue. Now, it is no longer just a Clipper issue. Whether Kahwi Leonard is on the Raptors or not has a huge circumstantial fallout in the Eastern Conference and then obviously like you know DeMar DeRozan is held up to a certain extent, for example. James Harden is hasn't done his business with the Cavs because they're waiting on things.

Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast

Aug. 7

NBA insiders: Updates on the biggest remaining NBA free agents

ESPN's NBA insiders came together to give updates on the top remaining free agents this season. Highlights include:

Multiple teams are pursuing Peyton Watson, including the Atlanta Hawks, LA Clippers, Milwaukee Bucks and Cleveland Cavaliers
The Detroit Pistons remain the favorite to sign Jalen Duren but the two sides are at an impasse
The Los Angeles Lakers are interested Jonathan Kuminga
James Harden is on track for a multi-year deal with Cleveland
DeMar DeRozan has drawn interest from the Miami Heat, Denver Nuggets, Washington Wizards and Cavaliers

Read more: Updates on the biggest remaining NBA free agents

Aug. 5

Brooks, Suns agree to three-year, $73 million extension
Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks agreed Wednesday to a three-year, $73 million contract extension through 2029-30, agent Mike George of Klutch Sports told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Credited with helping to establish a new culture in Phoenix, Brooks is coming off the best season of his nine-year career. He averaged a career-high 20.2 points to go with 3.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists for a surprise 45-win playoff team that maintained continuity throughout the offseason. In addition to bringing back Brooks, the Suns signed Collin Gillespie, Mark Williams and Jordan Goodwin to multiyear contracts and also acquired Miles Bridges and Luke Kennard.

Slater: Kings were actively shopping Sabonis at deadline, draft
ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that the Sacramento Kings were openly shopping forward Domantas Sabonis at the trade deadline and the 2026 draft.

The Kings nearly traded Sabonis to the Toronto Raptors at the deadline in February -- a move he would've welcomed, a source with knowledge of the situation said -- for a package that included RJ Barrett, but the Raptors were unable to get off the three-year, $84 million remaining on Jakob Poeltl's contract, which doomed the deal.
Sabonis had season-ending surgery on a partially torn meniscus later that month, and the Kings revisited trade talks surrounding him this summer. Perry visited with restricted free agent center Jalen Duren in early July and explored the idea of a sign-and-trade swap of big men, but the Detroit Pistons balked at the idea of losing Duren for Sabonis, league sources said.

There were predraft conversations about Sabonis with the Charlotte Hornets (who held pick Nos. 14 and 18) and at least one phone call with the Boston Celtics, team and league sources said, but nothing materialized. In Charlotte's case, the idea would've been to pair Sabonis with point guard LaMelo Ball, but the franchise instead opted to trade Ball for draft picks and lean further into a youth movement.

Read more: Darius Acuff is the Kings' future, but they still have to manage the present

July 30

Shelburne: The Cavaliers are still poking around with Peyton Watson
Appearing on ESPN's "NBA Today," Ramona Shelburne gave the latest on James Harden's free agency status after the All-Star declined a $42.3 million player option. "The Cavs are still poking around with Peyton Watson and I think that's why James has given them a lot of room to negotiate."

Shelburne: The Raptors have given zero indication of backing out of the Leonard trade
Ramona Shelburne appeared on ESPN's "NBA Today" to weigh in on the pending Aspiration investigation after Baxter Holmes reported today that the case could drag into 2027. "I haven't heard [the Raptors] trying to back out. I think the discussion is more of a leaguewide discussion."

July 28

76ers trade Broome, pick to Clippers for cash considerations
The Philadelphia 76ers are trading Johni Broome and a second-round pick to the LA Clippers for cash considerations, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Shams: Nuggets tweak asking price for potential Watson trade

Appearing on ESPN's "NBA Today," Shams Charania reported that the Denver Nuggets have lowered their asking price in a potential sign-and-trade of restricted free agent wing Peyton Watson. "The Nuggets initially had set a price this offseason of -- similar to the Walker Kessler deal -- two firsts and two swaps," Charania said. "Now that price is a really good high-level player as well as a first-round pick."

Shams: Wizards looking to add another scorer?

Appearing on ESPN's "NBA Today," Shams Charania reported that the Washington Wizards have had conversations with free agent guard DeMar DeRozan in recent days. The Wizards join the Miami Heat, Denver Nuggets and Cleveland Cavaliers among franchises to show interest in the six-time All-Star. DeRozan, who will turn 37 in August, was waived by the Sacramento Kings on July 6.

Warriors, Green agree to one-year deal

Draymond Green has agreed to return to the Golden State Warriors on a one-year, $27.7 million deal, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Green turned down his $27.6 million player option earlier this summer in a surprising move shortly before free agency kicked off. The decision created financial flexibility for Golden State, which was among the teams in the running to land LeBron James.

However, after James eventually decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Green and the Warriors moved forward on a new deal.

Will Towns get the max from Knicks?

Appearing on ESPN's "First Take," Brian Windhorst explained why the New York Knicks might hesitate on giving Karl-Anthony Towns a maximum contract extension of four years at $272 million.

"He's extension-eligible now. They could do this deal today. They haven't done the deal. They don't have an agreement on it. KAT is coming off the highest achievement of his career. He was awesome in the playoffs. He could look at the Knicks with a straight face and say 'I'm a max player. Pay me.' But in the modern era, you just have to be careful with this situation. ... Karl Towns absolutely earned and deserves a full max contract. If the Knicks give it to him, I'm not sure they're going to be able to keep this team together multiple years into the future."

Windhorst said that Knicks players such as Jalen Brunson and Mikal Bridges set the precedent of taking less money to help build out the roster, and New York might want Towns to do the same.

July 24

Shams: Inside Philly's recruitment of LeBron

Appearing on ESPN's "SportsCenter," Shams Charania detailed the discussions between the Philadelphia 76ers and LeBron James heading into the superstar's decision. "James was recruited by Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid -- he spoke to both of them. Jaylen Brown actually spoke to his agent, Rich Paul, during the process. And the only coach that LeBron James spoke to during this three-week-long process was Sixers head coach Nick Nurse."

Shelburne details conversation with Rich Paul

Appearing on ESPN's "NBA Today," Ramona Shelburne discussed what Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul told her Friday afternoon about LeBron James choosing the Philadelphia 76ers over a reunion with the Miami Heat or Cleveland Cavaliers. "When you've been to a place before, when you've won in a place before, if you go back, it may not be the same. You kind of want to leave those memories where they were."

NBA free agent frenzy 2.0 incoming?

With LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers, expect free agency to pick up.

Teams in discussion for James -- Cleveland, Denver, Golden State and Minnesota -- have roster spots to fill and key free agents to sign, notably James Harden, Draymond Green and Peyton Watson. Harden in Cleveland and Green in Golden State will play a role in how much financial flexibility each team has to offer available free agents.

The Cavaliers could have the $6.1 million taxpayer midlevel exception available, but only if Harden's next deal starts between $26 million and $28 million. Otherwise, the veteran minimum exception is the lone signing tool available to fill their two roster spots.
Golden State agreed to sign De'Anthony Melton to a two-year, $11.2 million contract early in free agency. The Warriors are hard-capped at the second apron and will likely have just the veteran minimum exception available after Green signs. They have three open roster spots.
The Nuggets, meanwhile, are in a holding pattern as it relates to restricted free agents Watson and Spencer Jones. Denver not only is a luxury tax team but will become the only team over the second apron if both players re-sign.
The Pistons, at least for now, do not have apron concerns as it relates to restricted free agent Jalen Duren. Detroit is $46 million below the luxury tax and $55 million under the first apron. There are financial concerns in the future, with Ausar Thompson eligible to sign a rookie extension this summer.

Other notable free agents to watch: DeMar DeRozan, Bradley Beal, Jonathan Kuminga and Russell Westbrook. Bennedict Mathurin is also a free agent, but the Clippers could match any offer sheet. -- Bobby Marks

Windhorst: Maxey connection helped lead LeBron to Philly

Appearing on ESPN's "First Take," Brian Windhorst detailed why the presence of point guard -- and fellow Klutch Sports client -- Tyrese Maxey was a major factor in LeBron James choosing to join the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency.

"LeBron [has a] comfort level and connection with Tyrese Maxey going back to when he was in college when he joined [Klutch]. Cleveland did not have that. Miami did not have that."

LeBron James signing with 76ers
LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million deal with a player option, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

By choosing the 76ers, James commits to a fourth NBA team as he searches for a fifth NBA championship before retirement.

James will hope to break a 43-year championship drought for the 76ers, much the same way he erased a 52-year streak without a title for the city of Cleveland when he won a championship with the Cavaliers in 2016.

Kram grades LeBron's new 2-year deal
Sports world reacts to LeBron's decision

Goodwill: James wanted Irving to join him on his new team
Senior writer Vincent Goodwill has a piece today on why LeBron James' storybook ending should be with the Miami Heat, not the Cleveland Cavaliers. In that piece, he drops a nugget on James angling for a deal to reunite with Kyrie Irving in Cleveland:

"League sources said James had been angling for former teammate Irving to join him in Cleveland, but the Dallas Mavericks have had no interest in engaging the Cavaliers in a trade, and Irving is believed to be comfortable where he is."
Read the full story here.

July 23

Shams: LeBron is not waiting for another domino
ESPN's Shams Charania joined "The Pat McAfee Show" to discuss how LeBron James and agent Rich Paul are not waiting for anything to happen to finally make their decision.

"My sources tell me that LeBron James, his agent Rich Paul ... they're not waiting for another domino right now. They're not waiting for Anthony Davis to get traded anywhere, they're not waiting for anyone else to move around anywhere."

Walsh back to Boston on three-year extension
Boston Celtics forward Jordan Walsh has agreed to a three-year, $15 million extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Walsh averaged 5.4 points and 4.0 rebounds per game last season.

July 22

Slater: Warriors still 'pessimistic' about LeBron choosing them
ESPN's Anthony Slater joined "NBA Today" to discuss how the Golden State Warriors are feeling in their pursuit of LeBron James.

"The Warriors are pessimistic that [signing LeBron James] will take place," Slater said. "Since the beginning, they've just really not thought they're at the top of the list. I talked to someone last night that basically said, 'They've given no sign or hint' that it's going to happen."

July 21

Shelburne: Duren talks at a 'standstill'

Free agent center Jalen Duren's contract talks are currently at a "standstill," sources told ESPN's Ramona Shelburne.

"I don't think [a deal] is going to happen anytime soon because I just talked to someone who said negotiations on Jalen Duren are at a standstill," Shelburne said on "NBA Today." "It could take deep into August, it could take quite a while."

Shelburne added that it will take a while because the Detroit Pistons "can't afford to lose" Duren but the parties can't agree on "what his value is."

McMenamin: Source said 'nothing happening today' on LeBron

ESPN's Dave McMenamin went on "SportsCenter" to discuss when LeBron James could announce his next team and end his free agency. He added that a source told him that it won't be happening today.

"I've been told by a source 'nothing happening today,'" McMenamin said. "People around the league, including commissioner Adam Silver, are trying to put pressure on the James' camp to make a decision."

McMenamin also added that James is still "weighing options" and there "isn't an elaborate rollout plan" for when James announces.

Paul on LeBron: 'Just have a little patience'

LeBron James' longtime agent, Rich Paul, went on "The Pat McAfee Show" to discuss the latest update on the superstar's free agency.

"Just have a little patience with him; obviously it's his choice," Paul said. "I have a job to do to set the table for him, but it's his choice. ... This is a very important choice for him; you cannot rush it. I think he's earned the right not to be rushed."

July 20

Shams: Paul says decision is up to LeBron, all the information is in

ESPN's Shams Charania went on "NBA Today" to discuss the future of LeBron James and the next step of his career.

"I spoke to Rich Paul, his longtime agent, this morning, and Rich Paul made it clear to me that it's LeBron James' decision right now," Charania said.

"All of the information is in, the teams are set, everyone has made their moves. There is no decision or choice yet. There's no timetable on a choice of a team. ... My understanding over the past couple weeks [is] that the focus has been primarily on the Eastern Conference teams, being Cleveland, Miami and Philadelphia.

Shams: Thybulle to Lakers on a one-year deal
Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that the Los Angeles Lakers and forward Matisse Thybulle have agreed to a one-year, $3.3 million deal.

July 19

Hawks land Dort in three-team deal
The Oklahoma City Thunder are sending veteran wing Lu Dort to the Atlanta Hawks in a three-team deal that sends three second-round picks to OKC, 2024 No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher to the Dallas Mavericks and Ryan Nembhard to Atlanta, sources told ESPN.

July 17

LeBron is 'trusting the process' with his decision looming
LeBron James hosted a live version of his podcast at Fanatics Fest NYC on Friday while the decision on where he'll spend his 24th season hangs over the league.

James said, "I want to compete at a high level. I want to join a franchise that shares the same models as myself. And that's like practicing championship habits everyday, but trusting the process more than anything".

Why Dolan is so worried about the second apron
The New York Knicks' championship parade has not even started, but there are already questions over whether finances will break up the roster.

"If we could bring back the whole team, exactly as is, why wouldn't you?" Knicks owner James Dolan said Wednesday on WFAN's "Carton Show." "I don't know if we'll be able to.

"We're willing to stretch, but there's certain things in the NBA that you'd have to be suicidal to do. One of them is the second apron. Cannot go into the second apron."

Including the 24th pick in next week's draft (June 23 and 24, 8 p.m. ET on ABC/ESPN), New York is $13 million below the second apron and has decisions with free agents Landry Shamet, Mitchell Robinson and possibly Jose Alvarado. (Alvarado has until Monday to decide on his $4.5 million option.) The entire starting five, meanwhile, is under contract through at least 2026-27. Karl-Anthony Towns is extension-eligible this summer and can become a free agent in the 2027 offseason if an agreement is not reached.

The second apron is a punitive luxury tax threshold restricting how teams add to their rosters in free agency, trades and the draft. In the case of the Knicks, the team would not be allowed to send cash in a trade, use the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception, aggregate salaries in a trade or use more than 100% of the traded player exception.

A team cannot trade its first-round pick seven years out if it finishes over the second apron in consecutive seasons, which no team has ever done. That same pick could be moved back to the end of the first round if a team finishes over the second apron in three out of four seasons. Luckily for Dolan and the Knicks, there are no rules that prohibit a team from retaining its own players.

New York can exceed the threshold to sign Robinson, Shamet and Alvarado. If the Knicks let the three players sign elsewhere, they would have their first-round pick (New York also has the 31st and 55th picks in the second round), the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception and $2.5 million veteran minimum exceptions available as replacements.

Since the apron rules were implemented before the 2024-25 season, Cleveland, Phoenix, Minnesota and Boston have finished the regular season over the second apron. The Knicks finished the past two seasons $53,000 and $370,000 below. Next offseason, New York is projected to be $31 million below the second apron with seven players under contract. -- Bobby Marks

stories.headline: DeGrom retires first 15 batters, Rodríguez hits 3-run homer off bullpen as Mariners beat Texas 4-3
stories.summary: — Jacob deGrom retired his first 15 batters and struck out 12 for his highest total since 2022 but Julio Rodríguez hit a go-ahead, three-run homer off Jakob Junis in a four-run seventh that lifted the Seattle Mariners over the Texas Rangers 4-3 Thursday.
stories.body:
SEATTLE -- — Jacob deGrom retired his first 15 batters and struck out 12 for his highest total since 2022 but Julio Rodríguez hit a go-ahead, three-run homer off Jakob Junis in a four-run seventh that lifted the Seattle Mariners over the Texas Rangers 4-3 Thursday.


DeGrom didn’t allow a hit until Cole Young singled on a line drive off the pitcher’s raised glove leading off the sixth. The two-time Cy Young Award winner struck out eight of his first nine batters for the fifth time and finished with his highest strikeout total since Sept. 19, 2022, for the New York Mets against Pittsburgh.


He left leading 3-0 after six innings due to groin tightness, manager Skip Schumaker said. But Junis (1-3) hit Randy Arozarena with a pitch leading off the seventh, then allowed Dominic Canzone’s RBI single and Cal Raleigh’s single. Rodríguez hit a first-pitch sinker for his 21st home run this season.


DeGrom gave up one hit in six scoreless innings with one walk.


Texas dropped three games behind AL West-leading Houston and two games back for the last AL wild card. Seattle trails by five games for the last wild card.


Logan Gilbert (12-9), who like deGrom attended Stetson, struck out 11 in seven innings and became Seattle’s first pitcher with consecutive double-digit strikeout games since James Paxton in 2018. The combined strikeouts were the most by starting pitchers in the major leagues this season.


Gilbert also made a sliding tag of Wyatt Langford off a throw from Raleigh after a pitch bounced away from the catcher in the seventh.


Andrés Muñoz walked a pair of batters with two outs in the ninth, then got Jake Burger to ground into a forceout for his 27th save in 36 chances. Young picked up the grounder behind second and just beat Evan Carter to the base, a call upheld in a video review.


Up next
Rangers: Start a three-game series Friday at Arizona, which starts RHP Merrill Kelly (9-13, 5.06).


Mariners: RHP George Kirby (9-11, 4.18) starts Friday at the Athletics, who open with LHP Jeffrey Springs (4-13, 6.02).

stories.headline: Fenerbahce president rejects coach Kartal's resignation after UCL draw
stories.summary: Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal announced his shock resignation after the 1-1 draw against Roma, but club president Aziz Yildirim said the coach remains in his position.
stories.body:
Fenerbahce coach İsmail Kartal stunned a post-match news conference following a 1-1 Champions League draw against Roma by announcing his resignation, a move that club president Aziz Yıldırım swiftly rejected.

"I have stepped down tonight," Kartal said. "I made this decision to clear the way for my club. I am resigning with the intention of never returning."

Kartal, who returned to the Istanbul side in June 2026 for his fourth stint, thanked the club for its support and congratulated his players on a match "we could have won," before adding that "from now on, to help Fenerbahçe, my footballers, I have resigned from my position, on the condition of never returning."

The announcement caught club officials entirely off guard, prompting Yıldırım to address the media minutes later to override the manager's decision.

"İsmail Kartal remains in charge. The club must support our coach. As long as I remain president, Kartal is the Fenerbahçe coach," Yıldırım said.

"There is no need for İsmail Kartal to say he will continue. I am his superior; I tell him, 'You will continue,' and that's that."

Playing in front of a sold-out Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium, Fenerbahçe marked their return to Europe's top-tier competition for the first time since the 2008-09 campaign.

Roma opened the scoring when Bryan Cristante capitalized with a low shot from outside the box in the 39th minute. Fenerbahçe responded early in the second half when left back Archie Brown expertly flicked the ball over the goalkeeper to equalize in the 48th minute.

Fenerbahçe will return to action on Monday to face Gaziantep FK in the Turkish Super Lig.

stories.headline: Šeško makes his case for Man United ahead of Manchester derby
stories.summary: Benjamin Šeško's form for Manchester United has given Michael Carrick a selection decision to make ahead of Sunday's Manchester derby.
stories.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Sabah FK didn't cause Manchester United any problems in their UEFA Champions League opener, but Benjamin Šeško has given Michael Carrick a headache before the Manchester derby.

The Slovenian striker followed up his goal at Everton on Sunday with another against the champions of Azerbaijan at Old Trafford on Thursday. It helped United to a comfortable 4-0 win while also making his claim to start against Manchester City on Sunday.

Šeško has had to wait his turn.

Injured in early May, he sat out all of preseason. A frustrating summer meant he was left on the bench for the first three Premier League games against Hull City, Ipswich Town and Everton.

A goal at Hill Dickinson Stadium earned him a start against Sabah, and he made the most of the opportunity when he collected Bryan Mbeumo's pass late in the first half, rounded the goalkeeper and scored for the second time in five days.

Šeško got 63 minutes before he was substituted for Joshua Zirkzee. It suggests that either the 23-year-old is still working his way back to full fitness or that Carrick is saving his legs for City. We'll find out Sunday.

"It's not an easy decision," Carrick said. "Of course it's not, but it's definitely one I'd prefer to have -- goals in the team and for the boys to be playing well.

"Sometimes it's going to be a start, sometimes it's going to be finishing the game, and we need that within the group from game to game over the season."

If nothing else, Šeško has given Carrick a decision to make. He will perhaps feel he has done enough to play against City, but the question is: Who does he replace?

Mbeumo scored a wonderful solo goal against Everton. Matheus Cunha got his first of the season against Sabah. Marcus Rashford, an unused substitute Thursday, was United's best player last weekend. If Šeško starts in the derby, one would have to drop out.

Perhaps in his favor is that he offers something different to Rashford, Cunha and Mbeumo. He gives United a focal point at No. 9 and a target in the box when the ball goes wide.

He also works hard. Shortly after halftime, he chased down a Sabah defender and wrestled the ball away, prompting a cheer from the Old Trafford crowd nearly as loud as the one when he scored.

"He definitely offers a different kind of threat," Carrick said. "I think that's kind of the beauty of it. That we know what Ben gives us, and there's not many around that give you what Ben does in terms of his physique, his physicality, playing on the last line, his speed to run in behind. He's a real threat.

"It's great to have him back at this level after working to get back to fitness. So, a couple of goals and good performances, good minutes for him. We're really pleased with the way he's gone."

Carrick can also be pleased with United's return to the Champions League. Playing in the competition for the first time since 2023, they dismantled Sabah, a club founded only nine years ago. Tougher tests lie ahead, but four goals and a clean sheet demonstrate a dream start.

"It was what we set out to achieve, really," Carrick said. "I think it was a good performance, individually, collectively, pretty much all the way through the game, from start to finish."

Šeško's form is a positive problem for United's head coach, but he has other selection issues to consider.

Luke Shaw started every Premier League game last season, but there has been debate over the summer about whether his body can cope with extra fixtures in Europe. The early answer is no.

Shaw came off in the 2-2 draw with Everton on Sunday because of cramps and missed training at Carrington on Wednesday morning. The official explanation was that he was given a "designated rest day." Not included in the squad to face Sabah, he had Thursday off, too. It wouldn't be a big issue if there was a designated backup.

Patrick Dorgu, who filled in against Sabah and got the assist for Cunha's opener, has been used as a winger since Carrick came in. Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot can play on the left but prefer the right. Harry Amass, a natural left back, is only 19. A summer bid for Newcastle United's Lewis Hall came to nothing.

Even in early September, it seems Carrick is already having to carefully pick and choose which games Shaw can play. He will hope the England defender is available again for the derby.

The task Sunday has been made more difficult by an uneven schedule that has given Enzo Maresca's team an extra two days to prepare. Carrick said this week it "wasn't ideal."

Preparations for the first Manchester derby of the season have at least been smoothed by a comfortable Champions League victory. Šeško got his goal and made his case to keep his place.

stories.headline: Team USA scores 108 in rout of Hungary to reach FIBA semis
stories.summary: The U.S. routed Hungary 108-56 to advance to the semifinals of the women's FIBA World Cup and stretched its winning streak in the tournament to 34 games.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- After a scare in the group phase against Italy, Team USA knew it wouldn't be able to play poorly in the knockout rounds of the FIBA World Cup if it wanted to come away with a fifth straight gold medal and 12th overall.

It was only the quarterfinals, but the U.S. responded to that challenge, putting together what the team viewed as its best performance of the tournament with a 108-56 drilling of Hungary. The Americans' 108 points and 31 assists were both records for a World Cup quarterfinal game.

Napheesa Collier led all scorers with 19 points -- a personal best with the senior national team -- followed by 15 from Rhyne Howard and 10 each from Kahleah Copper, Caitlin Clark and Jackie Young.

"We talked about just getting better with each game, and I think we did that today, especially with how we shared [the ball]," Howard said. "I think if we continue to play like that and continue to keep everybody on the same page, continue to move the ball, it's going to be really hard to stop us."

Added Collier: "We were moving the ball a lot. It wasn't one-on-one. We were looking for a great shot, not just a good shot, and so when we play that way, it's really fun. And I feel like our chemistry is building each game."

The U.S. will face either Spain or Australia in Saturday's semifinal, which will tip at 2 p.m. ET.

The Americans got out to a hot start, jumping ahead 36-12 at the end of the first quarter and leading 59-30 at the half. Their defense frustrated Hungary, which saw star post duo Dorka Juhasz and Virag Takacs-Kiss combine for just four points.

The U.S. had 25 of its 44 points off turnovers at the half, using defense to fuel offense on the other end.

"Everybody's just all dialed in offensively and defensively," said Angel Reese, who finished with nine points, six rebounds and three assists. "We talked about our keys, what it's going to take to win gold, and I think tonight we did everything that coach asked us to do."

Two games after Italy held the U.S. to 55 points, the Americans got mostly whatever they wanted offensively. Their 58.8% field goal percentage was their best clip of the tournament, and 12 3-pointers matched their tournament high after shooting 29% from deep in the group stage.

Team USA also won the inside battle Thursday, its 32 paint points at the half (52 overall) were more than the entire Hungary team had scored at that point.

"I feel like today was a really good one for us," Collier said. "We worked on some defensive schemes that we wanted to get better at, some offensive stuff that we wanted to clean up, and so I feel like we went out and executed that."

The 108 points marked the second most scored in a knockout game in World Cup history, behind only Brazil's 110 against the U.S. in the 1994 semifinals. The 52-point win margin was the second largest for a quarterfinal in World Cup history.

"I thought it started with our activity on the defensive end," coach Kara Lawson said. "And so our ability to turn them over, get out in transition, get some advantage plays, 2-on-1, 3-on-2, I thought gave us a lot of confidence early. And then our ability to shoot the 3-point shot ... we have a really good 3-point shooting team, and so I just thought that's what kind of jump-started us."

Lawson and the players agreed the performance was a product of their expedited chemistry-building finally starting to come into fruition. Unlike many national teams, the U.S. did not have a training camp or much prep time together before arriving in Berlin, last gathering as a group (and not its final roster) at the Final Four in April. They have now been together for about 10 days after leaving their WNBA teams.

"The more we play, the more comfortable we're getting with each other," said Young, the only American to hit double figures in each game this tournament. "And tonight we got the ball popping and we were able to get some easy buckets in transition."

Added Collier: "Today felt good, not just because of the score, but in the way that we were scoring as well."

stories.headline: How Holbrook inspired Newcastle's remarkable turnaround
stories.summary: Newcastle have scored an extra 12.3 points per game in 2026 compared to last year's wooden-spoon season, making for the fourth greatest improvement in history.
stories.body:
It took just one meeting for Justin Holbrook to start providing the belief for the fourth greatest attacking turnaround in Australian rugby league history.

With Newcastle players arriving for day one of pre-season, Holbrook's first move was to make clear last year's wooden spoon was irrelevant.

"There was obviously a lot of outside noise," five-eighth Fletcher Sharpe recalled.

"But Justin sat us down and said: 'Look, I don't really care about what happened last year - it's a new year and looking at the squad in front of me, I know we can take it all out'."

Brought in after Adam O'Brien's Newcastle exit, Holbrook immediately made his mark.

"He said we had to come together and buy into a style. And we can win the comp," added halfback Sandon Smith, who had worked with Holbrook at the Sydney Roosters.

"We bought in from November 1.

"It wasn't a moment throughout the season where we thought, 'Oh wait we can actually do this'. It was built into us from the first day."

Ahead of Friday night's elimination final against South Sydney, Holbrook's Newcastle turnaround is statistically one of the greatest in history.

And at the centre of it all is Newcastle's attack, with players quick to heap praise on assistant Stephen Hales.

Newcastle were kept scoreless in 11 halves of football in 2025, and had the NRL's worst attack.

Such is the improvement, the Knights are scoring an extra 12.3 points per game this year.

Only three sides in the game's 118-year history have had a greater increase, with Parramatta in 2001 the last side to have such a dramatic rise.

While Newcastle scored five tries from the other side of halfway last year, this year they have the most in the NRL with 30.

And 63 tries have also originated from outside the attacking 20-metre zone, compared to 18 last season.

"It's a fun style to play," Sharpe said.

"I remember at the start it seemed expansive and off the cuff, but the whole team bought into it.

"It allows our strike players on the edges to get plenty of ball and do their thing.

"It's probably a style not everyone plays, so it gives a difference and plenty of variety too, which you need at this time of year."

Remarkably, Newcastle are having less play-the-balls on the opposition tryline and running similar metres per game to last year.

But they are far more efficient and have a willingness to shift more often from their own end, giving their fast and powerful outside backs early ball to play with.

Wingers Dom Young and Greg Marzhew have 62 linebreaks and 44 tries between them.

Kalyn Ponga remains at the heart of the attack, but hooker Phoenix Crossland believes the rise of Sharpe has taken some pressure off the Newcastle No.1.

"We're attacking nothing like we used to last year," Crossland said.

"That happens with new coaches and fresh ideas, with boys buying into our system."

Impressive too is the fact the rise has come with Newcastle rarely at full strength, with Sharpe, Ponga and the now-injured Dylan Brown having stints out.

"The strength of our coaching staff is just letting individuals express themselves," Ponga said.

"Every team's got systems, but what they've done a good job of is just giving you that belief that you can play your footy.

"That's just the way that they frame everything up, that there's no limit on what you can be."

GREATEST YEAR-ON-YEAR ATTACKING IMPROVEMENTS:

Balmain (1944): +16.0 points per game

Eastern Suburbs (1935): +14.4

Parramatta (2001): +14.0

Newcastle (2026): +12.3

Manly (2021): 12.2

stories.headline: NBA punishes Clippers after Kawhi investigation: Top questions
stories.summary: A $30M fine. Five first-round picks taken away. Steve Ballmer suspended for a year. ESPN's NBA insiders break down the harshest punishment in league history.
stories.body:
The NBA has released the findings of its nearly yearlong investigation into the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, punishing both for violating salary cap circumvention rules when the team signed Leonard to an extension in 2021.

The league released a statement outlining that the investigation found "multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization."

Punishments include a $30 million fine and suspension for owner Steve Ballmer (one year), plus suspensions for team president of business operations Gillian Zucker (one year without pay) and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank (six months without pay).

The Clippers must also forfeit first-round picks in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033. Add the picks sent to the Oklahoma City Thunder in 2019 to acquire Paul George and secure Leonard's free agent signing, and LA will have given up a total of 10 first-rounders to acquire and retain Leonard.

On Thursday, The New York Times reported that the Justice Department had opened a criminal inquiry into the team's dealings with Leonard.

What does this all mean for Leonard, Ballmer and the future of the Clippers franchise? What will become of the agreed blockbuster trade to send the star forward to the Toronto Raptors?

ESPN's NBA insiders examine every angle of the league's shocking announcement.

How did the NBA come to its decision? How did it arrive at this punishment?
A significant part of this case appears to come down to the words "affirmative" and "responsive" as it pertained to how Leonard and the four companies arrived at endorsement deals.

In the investigator's report and in the Clippers' subsequent publicly released response, each side accuses the other of a flawed theory in how interactions between Leonard and the four companies were handled.

The Clippers believe their actions, connecting interested companies to Leonard for possible endorsement deals, constitutes a role as a middleman, which is permitted by league rules.

The investigators do not believe this and presented findings that they feel show the team flagrantly and repeatedly broke cap circumvention rules -- and that the Clippers took actions to make it appear, through emails, that they were acting within the rules.

The report repeatedly rejects the Clippers' argument that the connections were affirmative and, in some cases, cites admissions by the companies themselves.

The details make for compelling reading. In the case of scoreboard maker Daktronics, for example, the investigators accuse the Clippers of directing a kickback from a massive scoreboard contract for Intuit Dome to Leonard in the form of an endorsement deal and even setting the terms.

In other cases, the report cites the Clippers paying millions in "consulting" fees shortly after Leonard's endorsement deals were executed. The report doesn't specify exactly how the investigators acquired this information but repeatedly cites interviews with executives of the companies.

This punishment is in line with the penalty David Stern levied on the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2000 for executing an under-the-table deal with Joe Smith, which included five lost first-round picks, a then-record fine of $3.5 million, and owner and executive suspension and lost pay.

As for the size of the fine, the league appears to have imposed the maximum allowed fine for cap circumvention, $7.5 million, and imposed it for all four companies it believes the Clippers conspired with to circumvent cap rules, resulting in a compounded fine of $30 million. -- Brian Windhorst

Why did the NBA come down so hard on the Clippers if it didn't have "hard evidence" of salary cap circumvention?
The Wachtell report alleges Ballmer generally failed to "create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA's circumvention rules."

It also says he "knowingly sought to help [Kahwi] Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities and, in at least one instance, engaged in a significant act of team facilitation."

However, the report cites no specific evidence that would appear to implicate Ballmer directly. Instead, it connects the dots using the Clippers' knowledge of demands from Leonard's representative, Dennis Robertson, introductions between the Clippers and their sponsors, and communications regarding the latter.

The official reason the NBA gave for its conclusions and the level of punishment is the number and depth of the salary cap circumvention violations over the length of time the Clippers are accused of committing them.

According to investigators, contemporaneous notes from Frank indicate that Robertson complained to Ballmer that Zucker, the president of business operations, was making "introductions" for "bulls--- deals," and that "I have to get paid."

Investigators cited the same notes as saying Ballmer told Robertson that Clippers staff were "collective workers to try and help [Leonard] achieve his financial goals."

In addition to the notes written by Frank, who appears to have been given leniency for his cooperation, the report cites information that appears to have come from interviews with executives from the involved companies that created a compelling case.

The punishment was compounded by the Clippers being previous offenders during Ballmer's tenure as owner. They were fined $250,000 for a similar accusation involving DeAndre Jordan in 2015. There was also a 2019 investigation into Leonard's signing in which they were cleared of wrongdoing but subsequently warned and put through a seminar to remind them of the rules.

This penalty is indeed harsh, but it could have been worse.

In the case of Joe Smith and the Wolves in 2000, his contract was voided and his Bird rights were vacated.

Leonard will have to write a sizable check -- $700,000 -- but will not be suspended, and his contract and Bird rights remain unaffected.

The Clippers and the Raptors will be allowed to move forward in their trade process, one league source said. If the trade moves forward, LA will acquire two first-round picks in the deal. -- Windhorst

Do the Clippers have any recourse?

In its announcement, the NBA said the league and the NBPA have agreed on the penalties and that they are final and binding for all parties.

In a statement, however, the Clippers said they "intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process."

Ballmer's attorney, David Kelley, wrote an additional statement to the league, saying, "We are exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice."

Ballmer certainly has the means to commit resources toward clearing the team's name, though it's not immediately clear what those paths look like.

But it's not surprising that the Clippers would want to take this approach. They've been publicly and privately adamant from the start that they did not funnel money to Leonard through Aspiration, and one source close to the team with knowledge of the investigation said -- as ESPN previously reported -- that it would "fight that to the end," including through arbitration. -- Baxter Holmes

What does this punishment mean for the Clippers' future?
It means the Clippers have no access to first-round capital to use in a trade.

Trading center Ivica Zubac to the Indiana Pacers last February began the Clippers' process of rebuilding their draft assets, which had been depleted because of the trades for Paul George in 2019 and James Harden in 2023.

The Clippers acquired two picks in the deal, including one that resulted in the selection of Keaton Wagler with the No. 5 pick in this year's draft.

Before the NBA penalties were handed down, the Clippers had seven first-round picks over the next seven seasons, including four that were tradable. However, because of prior trades, LA had no control of its own first until 2030 (the Thunder have swap rights in 2027, the 76ers own the Clippers' 2028 pick and have swap rights in 2029).

By losing five firsts (the 2029 pick coming from the Pacers, plus their own picks in 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033), the Clippers' lone future picks are the less favorable of their own, Oklahoma City's, Denver's (if 6-30) in 2027 and the 2029 pick, none of which can be traded.

The Clippers, however, could be getting some draft relief relatively soon.

As part of the agreed-to trade to send Leonard to the Toronto Raptors, the Clippers were supposed to receive unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033.

The Clippers would not be allowed to trade those picks in future deals even if the Leonard trade goes through, because of the NBA's Stepien rule, which states that no team may trade a future first-round pick if the result would leave the team without first-round picks in any two consecutive future years. -- Bobby Marks

What does this mean for Steve Ballmer?
Ballmer has publicly and privately vowed to fight the NBA's decision, but it remains unclear what his options are outside of the court system. It's also unclear yet whether the NBA's yearlong suspension for Ballmer takes effect immediately, or whether he could ask the courts or an arbitrator to step in before it begins.

The alternate governor of the Clippers is Ballmer's business associate, Dennis Wong, who owns 1% of the team. Wong was named as an investor in Aspiration but is not mentioned in the release from the NBA on Wednesday.

This does not mean that Ballmer will have to sell the team, like former owner Donald Sterling did after being banned for life by NBA commissioner Adam Silver in 2014. Technically, Sterling did not have to sell the Clippers either. His wife, Shelly Sterling, decided to sell the team before the NBA's board of governors could vote to remove him as owner. -- Ramona Shelburne

Is there precedent for a team to be without its owner for an entire year?
Yes.

As part of the punishment from the Joe Smith salary cap circumvention case in 2000, the NBA suspended then-Minnesota Timberwolves owner Glen Taylor for one season. General manager Kevin McHale was also suspended for one season.

Other owners who have been suspended for a year or more for reasons other than salary cap circumvention include Donald Sterling (Clippers), Mark Stevens (Golden State Warriors) and Robert Sarver (Phoenix Suns). -- Marks

What does this mean for Lawrence Frank? Who is running the Clippers' front office in the interim?
The Clippers have not accepted the punishment and, therefore, have not named an interim leader of basketball operations.

However, it is likely that general manager Trent Redden, a respected veteran executive, will lead basketball operations.

If Frank is forced to sit out the next six months, the suspension will take him past the 2027 trade deadline but allow him to return in time for the draft, when the Clippers will have a first-round pick.

In that scenario, he will also be back in charge for 2027 free agency, when the Clippers are projected to have up to $50 million in salary cap space. -- Windhorst

Who is Gillian Zucker? What was her role?
Zucker has been the head of business operations for the Clippers since Ballmer bought the team, and she was the point person on all four deals between the team sponsors who also had endorsement contracts with Leonard.

The report from Wachtell comes down harshly on her, concluding "when interviewed, she made misleading and false statements to investigators."

In one particularly detailed section of the report, investigators wrote that when Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg told her he wanted to explore an endorsement agreement with Leonard, she "told Mr. Sanberg that she would enlist a particular business agent to assist Mr. Sanberg in structuring the agreement -- a business agent who was then under a retention agreement with the Clippers."

One day later, the report concludes that Zucker reached out to the business agent to help Sanberg.

That agent then emailed internal colleagues about the deal -- that Sanberg would offer Leonard $5 million, plus $7 million in stock, per year for four years as long as Leonard was with the Clippers.

The investigators concluded that Zucker improperly conveyed to the agent the proposed financial terms contained in this email.

The agent told investigators that neither the agent nor the agent's internal team came up with those terms. All relevant witnesses [including Zucker] agreed that Sanberg could not have come up with those terms because he didn't have experience structuring player endorsement deals. -- Shelburne

What does this mean for Dennis Robertson?
The NBA announced that Robertson, who has been a controversial figure in league circles for years, will face a five-year ban "from conducting business or otherwise engaging with NBA teams and their affiliates on behalf of or with respect to any player, employee, or other league or team personnel."

Robertson is Leonard's uncle and for years served as his business adviser.

He was also directly involved in Leonard's dealings with teams, including -- most notably -- his free agency negotiations with teams in 2019, during which Robertson made improper asks of the Clippers, including part ownership of the team, access to a private plane, a house and guaranteed off-court endorsement money, one source with direct knowledge of the talks previously told ESPN.

They were the same requests that, according to The Athletic, Robertson made of the Lakers and the Raptors. The Toronto Star reported Sept. 9 that Robertson also asked the Raptors for ownership stakes in outside companies and corporate sponsorship deals in which Leonard wouldn't have to do anything in return for the money.

These verbal requests fell outside the boundaries of the league's collective bargaining agreement, and word of them made waves around the league -- and reached the league office.

"As a direct result of Mr. Robertson's conduct on behalf of Mr. Leonard and the controversy surrounding the player's signing with the Clippers," the report from Wachtell Lipton noted Wednesday, "the NBA enacted a 'rules enforcement initiative' intended to promote better awareness, compliance, and enforcement of the circumvention rules.

"Among other things, this initiative included the adoption of the following rule:

"Teams are required to report to the league office any solicitation by a player of compensation or other benefits that are not authorized under the CBA. This includes any solicitation made by a player himself, by the player's agent, or by any other person acting (or purporting to act) on the player's behalf. Reports must be made even if the solicitation is rejected."

In July, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Leonard hired Harrison Gaines of Slash Sports as his new agent and as someone who would lead all his business affairs. Gaines replaced Leonard's previous agent, Mitch Frankel, and the informal role that Robertson previously held.

In his statement Wednesday, Leonard alluded to Robertson in the opening paragraph:

"Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family." -- Holmes

Is there precedent for the Clippers to get some of their picks back?
Yes.

In 2000, Minnesota lost its next five first-round picks for violating salary cap circumvention rules with its illegal attempt to sign Joe Smith.

Three years later, however, the NBA gave the 2003 and 2005 first-round picks back to the Timberwolves, leaving them without picks in 2001, 2002 and 2004. -- Marks
